text:
alex: quick idea: build a short-lived header to let clients opt into v3 behavior during the v4 cutover. header: `X-RW-Compat: v3` + `X-RW-Compat-TTL: seconds`. keep it temporary and observable.

marta: sounds pragmatic. two immediate Qs: 1) tenant-level opt-in vs request-only header? 2) what happens on streaming routes?

alex: proposal: tenant opt-in gate (default off) + request header with TTL. router will reject for streaming endpoints. that avoids streaming translation risk.

samir: perf caution: any proxy-side translation adds CPU + ~1-3ms. at high QPS that compounds. we should limit per-tenant usage and measure impact before wide roll.

alex: agreed. limit: header honored only if tenant flag on and the tenant is inside a migration window. outside window -> 403. header must include TTL and we reject headers > 600s.

marta: we need telemetry keys: `compat.header.used`, `compat.result` (translated|passthrough|rejected), and per-version counters. also add a deprecation tag on traces.

samir: streaming exclusion: return 400 for POST /v4/stream or /v4/chatstream with migration link, better than silently translating. streaming frames are too brittle to rewrite safely.

alex: implement a tiny service `compat-bridge` that lives in front of the runtime. for non-streaming routes it rewrites request shape and headers before forwarding. fallback behavior should be configurable per-tenant: fail-open (warn header) vs fail-closed (reject). default = fail-open.

marta: include response header `X-RW-Compat-Result` so customers and infra can see when translation happened. example: 
```http
POST /v4/generate
X-RW-Compat: v3
X-RW-Compat-TTL: 60
Content-Type: application/json

{"prompt":"write a haiku"}
```
response should include `X-RW-Compat-Result: translated` when applied.

samir: billing note: translation may change token counts (prompt expansion, instruction folding). ensure billing pipeline uses post-translation token deltas and attributes correctly. also add regression tests to avoid double-counting.

alex: will add billing integration and regression tests to RFC. also plan perf microbench: target p50 added latency <2ms at 10k RPS, p95 <7ms.

marta: add security sign-off for translation rules (may touch PII). require a short review for each tenant rule change.

samir: operational concern: cache rules in-memory for low latency, but ensure invalidation path when tenant toggles opt-in or window. maybe use a short TTL + manual invalidation hook.

alex: yep. mapping service with local cache + push invalidation. also emit metrics for cache hit/miss.

marta: one more: define clear sunset policy in the RFC: escape-hatch expires after X days from tenant opt-in or from cutover date. require explicit extension requests via support. no permanent escapes.

samir: SGTM. and add a canary plan: enable for a single low-volume tenant first, watch errors/latency/token deltas then increase.

alex: I'll draft RFC with header semantics, tenant gating, TTL rules, streaming exclusions, fail-open/fail-closed toggle, telemetry keys, billing plan, security signoff, cache invalidation, perf targets, and canary rollout plan. will create staging tickets and a perf-run ticket.

deploybot: rolling deploy of compat-bridge v0.1 to staging at 1718760005 :rocket:

marta: thanks. this feels like a pragmatic short-term shim that avoids long-lived compatibility debt if we enforce TTLs & migration windows. :thumbsup:
